cards.note: Buildings with features similar to Alpine architecture, such as white walls with brown wooden details are commonly found in and around the Smoljan region in the south. Lots of pine trees are also commonly seen.

This trekker is found on the Balkan mountain. The trekker is divided in 2 parts, you can see huge green lush mountains with exposed grey rock in the northern half. The southern half is just a forest with steep elevation.

The 11 and 15 that goes from Oryahovo to Vratsa has this distinct road with a tremendous amount of black dots on it (idk what its called). This kind of road is also found in the south on the 6 between Radomir and Izvor. And a small part of the 1 around Mursalevo. (mountainous = south, flat = north, beware that the 15 towards Vratsa gets huge mountains towards the south)

NOTE: There are a very few other roads elsewhere in Bulgaria that also have the dots but are more greyish and are less distinct. Make sure the road really has that distinct look with the clear black dots on them.

This antenna with unpeeled tape at the top, resulting in a bulkier antenna tip, can be found in the Varna Province. Coverage with this antenna is exclusively in March, resulting in a dead winter look.
Dense pine trees are super common in the south of Bulgaria, specifically in the province of Smolyan, the southern half of Pazardzhik, East Blagoevgrad and small areas around them.

This long stretched region south of the Balkan Mountains can be recognized by the flat agriculture landscape, with a big mountain ridge to the north and smaller mountains/hills to the south. You can also sometimes see tiny hills/mountains to your east/west. (Tip for memorizing: From Rozino to Sliven).

The region south/south-east of Sliven has little to no hills to the south, but still has the distinct mountain ridge to the north aswell as small hills towards the east/west.

NOTE: There are a few other smaller regions with smaller mountains that can have a similar appearance, their either more towards the west or east.

East Dobrich is by far the flattest region of bulgaria, it will either be completely flat or you will notice very little elevation. Rows of trees are commonly seen next to the road and in the distance. Landscape itself is very agriculture and you will almost never see hills in this region (they become more common towards the west).

Also wind turbines can often be seen towards the south-east.
Locations with an invisible Generation 4 Street View car can be found along the North and West borders of Bulgaria, as well as the northern half of the coast.

Generation 3 locations with a taped long antenna and visible white car can be found in Stara Zagora, and rarely a few small roads in Plovdiv and Burgas.

NOTE: This combination of car and antenna can be found more commonly in other European countries as well. Make sure to use other clues.

This trekker is found on the Musala mountain. You can often see a mountain ridge to the west, part of the trekker is on the ridge itself. Other mountains are seen on the east. Its very rocky with lots of small pine trees.

The old town of Nessebar, and to a lesser extent Sozopol, can be recognised by the well-preserved old buildings made of a combination of unpainted stone, white stone walls and brown wood. Most of the streets are paved with cobblestone.
This trekker is found on top of Pirin National Park. It has a tremendous amount of white/grey rocks laying around. With lots of small bushes.

This big region surrounding Plovdiv can be recognized by the very large flat agriculture landscape, and you can almost always see big mountain ridges to the north and the south. Its possible that you can't see the mountains on one side because your too far north or south. But even then its still recognizable. Also the mountains to the south are bigger than the mountains north.

The region around Pazardzhik can also look quite similar but has random hills and is less flat.
Plovdiv has these 2 unique street signs. The one on the left is more common.

The towering mountains of Pirin and Rila National Parks can be recognised by the tall pyramid-shaped peaks, and can be seen from a few different vantage points in Blagoevgrad, Kyustendil and Sofia Provinces.

A red Generation 4 Street View car is mostly found in central and southeastern Bulgaria.

This car can be found with and without an antenna.

Generation 3 coverage with a piece of tape on a short antenna can be commonly found in the eastern part of Bulgaria.

NOTE: Tape antennas can very rarely appear in other provinces, the only provinces where it’s never found are Vratsa, Montana, Pazardzhik and Smolyan.
You can often see this big white cross on the top of a mountain to the north/east in and around Sliven. It can be a little hard to see sometimes so make sure to zoom in and identify it.

White street signs with two red strips (can rarely be blue or green); one covering the bottom and one covering part of the top, can be found in Sofia.

NOTE: You can also find other types of street signs in Sofia.
Brown street signs with bright yellow text can be found in Stara Zagora.

The Vitosha Mountain south of Sofia can be recognized by its huge and long dome-like shape. You can often see tall buildings beneath it and it can be seen from far away. A ridge of mountains can also be seen in the south and the landscape around it is pretty flat and agriculture.
The mountains overlooking Vratsa from the southwest have a very distinct “bumpy” shape, and can be seen from afar in the province.
Wind turbines are most common in Dobrich Province, and usually towards the coast.
